name: International Sign
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kusters, Annelies. 2026. The Paradox of International Sign. Deaf Studies and Sign Linguistics. Bristol: Multilingual Matters. DOI 10.21832/9781800413917 (open access, Zenodo record 22799468).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic/sociolinguistic monograph; all 13 'stress' hits are non-technical; one passage (ch. 4) says admired on-stage IS signers have 'effective intonation and well-paced prosody'; fingerspelling 'is generally not a significant feature of its phonology' (ch. 3). Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Nana Gassa Gonga, Aurélia Armelle. 2025. Linguistic insights on interpreting to international sign (IS): IS produced by interpreters, evidence for a language-like system. Radboud Dissertation Series. Nijmegen: Radboud University Press. 226 pp. DOI 10.54195/9789465151274 (CC BY-NC-ND).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on word/sign stress. Ch. 1 background (p. 23) only says non-manual elements 'are equally critical phonological components. These features add prosody and grammatical information, including marking negation, questions, and emphasis'; the seven 'stress' hits are the ordinary verb (stresses the need, stressing the iconicity) and one remark about the spoken presenter's prosody. Emphasis in IS is described as lexical sign + facial expression ('IS emphasis strategies (see McKee and Napier, 2002)', p. 137), a discourse-level device, not sign-level stress placement.

sources.citation: Bickford, Albert & Rachel Rosenstock. 2008. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2008-025 and Request for New Language Code Element [ils] International Sign. SIL International (adopted 2009-01-16).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says 'Grammar is typical of sign languages generally' (p. 3 of the change request) and that Gestuno 1975 presented 'No grammar'; IS 'is more properly considered a pidgin, rather than a full language' (new-code form p. 2). Gives the IS bibliography to 2008 (Allsop, Woll & Brauti 1994/5; Webb & Supalla 1994; Supalla & Webb 1995; Woll 1990; Moody 1989, 2002; McKee & Napier 2002; Coppock 1990a,b; Bergmann 1990).

sources.citation: Monteillard, Nathalie. 2001. La langue des signes internationale. Aperçu historique et préliminaires à une description. Acquisition et interaction en langue étrangère 15: 97-115. DOI 10.4000/aile.1347.
sources.note: Open on OpenEdition but the site's Anubis bot-wall blocked automated download (only the challenge page saved); read through direct download. Sections: Gestuno; 'préliminaires à une description' (one-handed vs two-handed sign types, body location of signs); conclusion. Per the downloaded text, no treatment of phonologie, prosodie, accent or rythme.
